items: Nan re-voiced to the clip (same voice, Vindemiatrix): four quick, clipped takes, best one fitted. 'Poor' on her first opening, the pause on her lip closure, 'bastard' as she reopens, finished by 3.84 s (was 4.6 with a trailing breath).

If it still reads wrong: her mouth draws only ONE syllable for 'bastard', so the '-stard' lands as her lips close. Retiming the voice can't beat that. The real fix is LatentSync, which redraws her mouth to the voice (about a 10 GB install, local GPU, no Flow credits). Say if you want it.
Or say 'it's done' and it goes into Premiere.

replies.at26: Done: real headline, newsprint style, 0.5–3.2 s, below his face; everything else unchanged. Source: ITV News, 22 Mar 2024 (the article's own title; the headline doesn't name him).
replies.at429: Done: effects lowered 8 dB everywhere (-30 → -38 LUFS), about 20 dB under both voices now.
replies.at52: Done: on screen 2 s longer, 0.5–5.2 s, so it's still up as the narrator says '£100,000 a year'.
replies.at627: Fixed with a new clip: Flow allowed 'Poor bastard' after all with a bare prompt (the first refusal was the long prompt). Her lips close for the P and the b, and the voice now lands on both; checked frame by frame.
replies.at589: Re-voiced to her mouth: four new takes directed short and clipped; take b fitted at x1.10. 'Poor' and the b closure now match; the '-stard' still ends ~0.2 s after her mouth (the picture only draws one syllable). If that still shows, LatentSync is the fix.
